text:
Tye Kartye is the kind of story a good season needs. Undrafted, a Seattle depth winger until this year, he's now playing 16:48 a night for the Rangers, up from under 12 minutes last season, with 14 points in 21 games and a spot on the power play he never used to see. Sports Illustrated has started calling him a building block.

This qualifies as a breakout by our rules, and the underlying numbers back it up. His own chances have more than doubled, 1.04 expected goals (the quality of chances) per 60 against 0.46 last season, and the Rangers take 57% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. Seven goals on 6.1 expected is fair finishing, and if anything his linemates have been unlucky: the team has scored 4.7 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him out there.

He still plays like the grinder who earned the job, with 57 hits in 21 games, and our model compares him to penalty-killing forwards like Connor Dewar and Jordan Martinook. Our talent range has him around 53 points for the season. Watch whether the power-play time sticks once Sean Durzi is back.
